description: Is a drafted customer-support reply safe to send without a person reading it? Enterprise accounts always get a human with no model call; a reply is held when the tone is risky, reviewed when it makes a commitment, and auto-sent only when it is confidently a routine answer.

reply_kind.instructions: What kind of message is the drafted reply in `draft.text`?

ANSWER.what: Answers a how-to or status question with facts and no promise.
examples: You can export your data from Settings, Export.

APOLOGY.what: Apologises for a problem or delay.

OFFER.what: Offers or promises money, credit, a replacement, a deadline or a policy exception.
examples: We will refund the last two invoices.

contains_commitment.instructions: Does the draft in `draft.text` promise or imply anything the company must then deliver?

true.what: It commits to a refund, credit, replacement, date, legal position or exception.

false.what: It only informs, or points to existing documentation.

tone_risk.instructions: Would a reasonable customer find the draft in `draft.text` dismissive, blaming, sarcastic or hostile?

true.what: Dismissive, blaming, sarcastic or hostile in places.

rules.reason: Enterprise accounts always get a person.
The draft may read as hostile or dismissive; do not send.
The draft may make a commitment or concede fault; a person checks it.
Confidently a routine answer with no commitment and no tone risk.

default.reason: Not clearly routine; a person checks it.

on_unavailable.reason: The model could not be consulted; a person checks it.
